## PHASE: reviewer
## ISSUE: 247

### Issue Details
## Issue #247

## Parent

#242 ([PRD] Cross-Module Generalization: Customer Component + Full POS Line Items)

## What to build

Upgrade the POS frontend cart store and UI components to support all three line item types (part, labor, bicycle). The cart Zustand store (`pos/store.ts`) is updated from flat part-only structure to discriminated union. Cart display component renders appropriate fields per type. UseCart hook handles add/remove/update across all types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `client/src/features/pos/store.ts`: cart line item type updated to discriminated union supporting part/labor/bicycle
- [ ] `useCart` hook: add/remove/update operations work for all three line item types
- [ ] `CartDisplay.tsx`: renders appropriate fields per line item type (part shows partId/name, labor shows service/minutes, bicycle shows template info)
- [ ] Unit tests for cart operations with each line item type
- [ ] End-to-end demo: add labor and bicycle items to POS cart, verify correct rendering, checkout succeeds

## Blocked by

- #244 (Create Shared Line Item Variant Definitions)
- #246 (POS Service Layer: Labor + Bicycle Line Items)

## Out of Scope

The following are **explicitly NOT part of this issue** — they require separate slices/issues:

| Area | Reason |
|------|--------|
| Labor/bicycle search UI components | PRD (#242) defers "Line item UI components (parts/labor/bicycle sections)" to a later pass. PartsSearch.tsx remains parts-only for this issue. |
| New catalog API endpoints | No labor-services search route exists on the server yet; bicycle-templates has display pages but no POS-specific search endpoint. |
| Removing duplicate store file | `hooks/useCart.ts` is an orphaned duplicate (only its test imports it). Consolidation is a separate cleanup task. |

<!-- AGENT-FINDINGS-START -->
## Agent Findings

### Archivist — 2026-06-01

#### ⚠️ Duplicate Store Files: `store.ts` vs `hooks/useCart.ts`

Two nearly identical Zustand stores exist, both exporting `useCartStore`:

| File | Imports By | Math Source | Types Location |
|------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `client/src/features/pos/store.ts` | **All production components** (6 imports) | Inline `computeLineTotals()` function | Defines types inline (`CartLineItem`, `CheckoutPayload`, etc.) |
| `client/src/features/pos/hooks/useCart.ts` | Only its own test file | Shared lib: `@shared/lib/pricing.js` | Imports from `../types.js` |

**Key difference:** `hooks/useCart.ts` uses the shared pricing library and imports types from `types.ts`, while `store.ts` has everything self-contained. All production code (`PartsSearch.tsx`, `CartDisplay.tsx`, `PaymentDialog.tsx`, `PaymentForm.tsx`, `PosPage.tsx`, `checkout.ts`) imports from `../store`.

**Recommendation:** Update `store.ts` (the live one). The `hooks/useCart.ts` is an orphan — builder should note it exists but not modify it unless explicitly asked to consolidate. Tests in `__tests__/useCart.test.ts` test the hooks version, while `__tests__/store.test.ts` tests the production version.

#### 📋 CheckoutPayload Type Update Required

Current `CheckoutPayload` (in both `types.ts` and `store.ts`) is parts-only:
```typescript
lineItems: Array<{
  partId: string        // ← always present, no lineType discriminator
  quantity: number
  unitPriceNet: number
  vatRateId: string
  description: string
}>
```

Server-side expects discriminated union per `shared/validations/sales.ts`:
```typescript
cartLineItemSchema = z.discriminatedUnion(lineType, [
  partLineItemVariant.toSchema(),    // { lineType: part, partId, ... }
  laborLineItemVariant.toSchema(),   // { lineType: labor, laborServiceId?, minutesWorked?, ... }
  bicycleLineItemVariant.toSchema(), // { lineType: bicycle, bicycleId?, bicycleBrand?, ... }
])
```

**Action:** `CheckoutPayload.lineItems` must become an array matching the discriminated union shape from `shared/validations/sales.ts`. The `getCheckoutPayload()` method in store needs to map cart items to this new shape.

#### 📋 Shared Types Reference

| File | What It Defines | Relevance |
|------|----------------|-----------|
| `shared/types/sale.ts` | `SaleLineItem` interface with all 3 types (partId, laborServiceId, bicycle fields) | Source of truth for DB-backed line item shape |
| `shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts` | Part/Labor/Bicycle variant objects with Zod schemas | Used by server validation; frontend should mirror these shapes |
| `shared/lib/pricing.ts` | Shared `computeLineTotals()` function | hooks/useCart.ts already uses this; store.ts has its own copy |

#### 📋 CartDisplay Rendering Per Type

Current `CartDisplay.tsx` renders a single row format assuming part-only items (shows `partId`, barcode, quantity ± buttons). For discriminated union:

- **Part items**: Current rendering is sufficient (name, price, qty, VAT)
- **Labor items**: Need to show service name/description, minutes worked, hourly rate snapshot
- **Bicycle items**: Need to show brand, model, year, color, frame size

The `CartLineItemRow` sub-component will need a discriminated render (e.g., `switch (item.lineType)`).

#### 📋 Relevant Files Summary

| File | Purpose | Change Needed |
|------|---------|---------------|
| `client/src/features/pos/store.ts` | Production Zustand store | **PRIMARY** — add discriminated union types, update actions for labor/bicycle |
| `client/src/features/pos/types.ts` | Shared POS types (VAT_RATES, CartLineItem, CheckoutPayload) | Update `CartLineItem` to discriminated union; update `CheckoutPayload` line items shape |
| `client/src/features/pos/hooks/useCart.ts` | Orphaned duplicate store | **DO NOT MODIFY** — orphan file, only tested by its own test |
| `client/src/features/pos/components/CartDisplay.tsx` | Cart UI rendering | Add type-discriminated rendering for labor/bicycle rows |
| `client/src/features/pos/__tests__/store.test.ts` | Tests for production store | Add tests for labor/bicycle line item operations |
| `shared/types/sale.ts:31-48` | `SaleLineItem` interface | Reference for field names/shapes across all 3 types |
| `shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts` | Shared variant definitions | Reference for discriminated union structure |

<!-- AGENT-FINDINGS-END -->

## Parent PRD (#242)

## Problem Statement

The four core transaction modules — POS, Repairs, Orders, and Quotes — each implement their own customer selection logic, line item validation schemas, and UI components independently. This creates duplication (~150-200 lines of near-identical search/debounce/dropdown code per module), inconsistent behavior (customer required in some modules but optional in others), and makes cross-module changes error-prone because the same concept is implemented differently four times.

POS currently only supports parts-only line items, making it unable to serve as a reference implementation for the other three modules which already support labor and bicycle line types. The validation schemas are scattered across separate files with no shared variant definitions, meaning any change to how a "part" or "labor" line item works must be replicated manually in up to four different schema files.

## Solution

Make POS the clean reference implementation by:
1. Extracting the customer selector into a single shared component used by all four modules
2. Creating shared line item variant definitions that each module composes into its own validation schema
3. Upgrading POS to support all three line item types (part, labor, bicycle) matching the domain model already present in the database

## User Stories

1. As a cashier using POS, I want to select an existing customer or leave it blank for walk-in sales
2. As a cashier using POS, I want to add parts from catalog via barcode scan or search
3. As a cashier using POS, I want to create special (ad-hoc) products when item not in catalog
4. As a cashier using POS, I want to add labor services with hourly time tracking
5. As a cashier using POS, I want to add bicycle line items referencing templates
6. As a repair technician, I want optional customer on repair intake for walk-in repairs
7. As a repair technician, I want CRUD line items on repairs incrementally
8. As a salesperson, I want optional customer on orders for walk-in orders
9. As a salesperson, I want atomic parts/labor/bicycle line items when creating order
10. As a salesperson, I want optional customer on quotes for anonymous estimates
11. As a salesperson, I want CRUD line items on quotes incrementally
12. As a developer, I want shared CustomerSelector component used by all modules
13. As a developer, I want shared line item variant definitions in one file
14. As a shop owner, I want every part sold to reference catalog entry

## Implementation Decisions

### Module 1: Shared Customer Selector Component (Frontend)
- Extract from POS into `client/src/features/customers/components/CustomerSelector.tsx`
- Props: `{ customerId?: string | null, onSelect, required?: boolean }`
- All four modules import and use this component

### Module 2: Shared Line Item Variant Definitions (Shared Validations)
- Create `shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts` with part/labor/bicycle variants
- Each module composes its own discriminated union from shared variants

### Module 3: Customer Optional Across All Modules (Backend Schemas)
- Repairs: allow customerId null without existing/new customer path
- Orders: customerId changed to nullable optional
- POS/Quotes already optional — no change

### Module 4: POS Service Layer Upgrade (Backend)
- `createDirectSale()` handles labor and bicycle line items
- Stock validation only on part-type items

### Module 5: POS Cart Store Upgrade (Frontend)
- Cart supports discriminated union of all three line item types
- Cart display renders appropriate fields per type

## Testing Decisions

1. Shared Customer Selector — unit tests for selection callback, null handling
2. Line Item Variant Schemas — unit tests for each variant valid/invalid inputs
3. POS Sales Service — integration tests: parts-only, labor, bicycle, mixed-type cart
4. Orders Schema — unit test customerId optional

## Out of Scope

1. Line item UI components (parts/labor/bicycle sections) — deferred to later pass
2. Fixed-price labor services — hourly stays core
3. Bicycle inventory management — templates only
4. Inline customer creation at POS — walk-in only
5. Multi-payment split, invoicing, void auth guard

# Project Glossary

**Last Updated:** 2026-05-21  
**Maintained By:** Development Team  
**Status:** ✅ Current  

---

## Purpose

This glossary defines project-specific terminology to ensure consistent understanding across the team and AI agents. Terms here reflect the **POS domain**, not template scaffolding.

---

## A

### App Event / Domain Event
A named signal fired via `appEvents.emit()` to communicate cross-cutting side effects (notifications, gamification points) from features to the app shell. Events are decoupled — features don't know who listens. Payloads are typed via an event registry.

---

## C

### Customer
Shop customer with contact information (`firstName`, `lastName`, optional `email`/`phone`). Can be unattached to a sale (walk-in). Stored in the `customers` table.

### Direct Sale
The core POS transaction: customer selects parts from stock, pays via single method, sale is created atomically with stock deduction. `sourceType='direct_sale'`. This is V0's only supported sale type.

---

## E

### Event Listener
A function registered in a feature's `listeners/` directory that responds to domain events fired by other features or the app shell. The app shell collects and calls all listener registration functions on mount.

---

## F

### Feature
A self-contained unit of functionality spanning types, validations (Zod schemas), UI components, routes, stores, and services. Features own their code but share a common structural template. Examples: `pos/`, `catalog/`, `product-finder/`.

**Note:** The current architecture uses feature-based folder organization (`features/<name>/`), but the target state is **flow-first consolidation** where core transaction logic moves into deep modules (e.g., `sale.service.ts`) rather than scattered across multiple features. See `clean-structure-decision.md` in planning notes.

### Feature Contract
A document specifying a feature's scope, requirements, architecture, and acceptance criteria before implementation begins. Created via the `to-prd` skill and published as a GitHub Issue.

---

## G

### Golden Copy Pattern
The practice of using one existing feature module as a structural reference template for new features, ensuring consistent patterns across modules. Currently based on the sales feature structure.

---

## L

### Layer
A logical separation of concerns in the codebase:
- **Presentation Layer**: UI components (React)
- **Business Logic Layer**: Services and route handlers
- **Data Access Layer**: Repositories (Drizzle queries)

**Rule:** Request flow is Routes → Services → Repositories. No layer skips.

### Line Item
A single part on a sale with `partId`, `quantity` (always 1 in V0), `unitPriceNetCents`, and `vatRateId`. Stored in the `saleLineItems` table.

---

## P

### Part (Product)
Sellable inventory item stored in the `parts` table. Has a name, optional SKU/barcode, selling price (`unitPriceNetCents`), cost price (`costPriceCents`), and denormalized stock count (`quantityOnHand`). The domain term is "part"; some code uses "product" interchangeably.

### Sale
Core POS transaction record. Contains `sequenceNumber`, optional `customerId`, `status` (active/voided), financial totals, and a list of line items. Created atomically in one database transaction.

### Sale Cart
Client-side Zustand store holding part line items (`partId`, `quantity`, `unitPriceNetCents`, `vatRateId`) awaiting checkout. Lives entirely in the browser until submitted via POST to `/api/sales`.

---

## S

### Sequence Number
Human-readable document numbers (`SA-0001`, `INV-0001`) generated via a dedicated `sequences` table with atomic increment. One sequence per document type (`sale`, `invoice`). Avoids race conditions vs MAX+1 approach.

### Slice
A vertical slice of work: one complete user story touching all layers (types → DB → API → UI). Used by the planner and to-issues skills to break down features into independently shippable units.

### Stock Movement
Immutable audit row recording every inventory change in the `stockMovements` table. Fields: `partId`, `quantityDelta` (+/-), `reason` (`sale`, `purchase`, `adjustment`), optional `referenceId`. 

**Rule:** `quantityOnHand` on parts is denormalized — always compute as `SUM(quantityDelta)` for accuracy. Stock movements are the source of truth.

### Store
Zustand store. Global stores are cross-cutting only (sidebar, theme). Feature stores live within their feature directory and manage feature-specific state.

---

## V

### Validation Schema
Zod schemas that define expected input shapes and provide runtime type checking. Shared between frontend (form validation) and backend (request validation) via the `shared/validations/` package. Server re-exports them as a "golden copy" to prevent schema drift.

### Voided Sale
A sale marked `status='voided'`. No stock reversal, no payment unallocation. Used to fix cashier errors. Manager-only in production (authorization deferred for V0). Implemented via one PATCH endpoint with zero schema changes.

---

## W

### Walk-in Sale
A sale with no customer attached (`sales.customerId` is NULL). Anonymous transaction. Supported alongside named-customer sales in V0.

---
